title: Thank your teachers
intro: In this tradition, the teacher is honoured as a form of the divine: the one who removes the darkness of not knowing. This practice is gratitude for everyone who has taught you anything.
offering: Thanks, said or written to a teacher.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Sit comfortably, with your back upright and soft. Follow the circle: in as it grows, out as it settles. Never strain.

steps.title: The teacher as divine
steps.text: The best known verse to the teacher.

steps.title: The one who opened my eyes
steps.text: A verse of gratitude: my teacher opened my eyes with the light of knowledge.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Repeat this verse to Dakshinamurti, the teacher of all worlds.

steps.title: Your teachers
steps.prompt: Who taught me something that changed me? What would I say to them?

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Read the closing prayer once, slowly. Then sit for one more breath before you return to your day.

after: Guru Purnima, the full moon of Ashadha, is the teachers’ day.
